title: kube: print secret removal errors on kube down
body:

and ensure you follow them before signing off your commits.

- [ ] All commits pass `make validatepr` (format/lint checks). Local `gofumpt` and `golangci-lint` 2.15.0 on `./cmd/podman/kube/...` are clean. `make validatepr` was not run here.
- [x] [Release note](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/guide/release-notes.md) entered in the section below (or `None` if no user-facing changes)

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
kube down prints a secret removal failure on its own, including when pod removal succeeded.
```

`podman kube down` and `podman play kube --down` stored the last secret removal error and then tested the pod removal error before printing it. `PrintErrors` writes every earlier error and returns the last one, so one secret failure never reached stderr when the pods were removed. When a pod failed and the secrets were removed, stderr also gained `Error: %!s(<nil>)`.

The secret line now uses the secret error. Pod stop, pod removal, and volume removal are unchanged. Volume removal is still the error returned to the command. Pod removal errors stay printed and are still not returned, and secret removal follows that same pattern.

No open issue matched this. The wrong condition landed in `2659a3228a` (2023-02-16), "kube: rm secret on down, print secret on play".

comments.body: I'd generally prefer an E2E test, where we actually have a separate process and don't need hacks to capture STDOUT/STDERR, over the existing unit test

The remote client rejected the secret error string from the service, so `kube down` exited 125 before it could print that error. `SecretRmReport` now decodes the string. The e2e covers both the local and remote clients.
